topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames complement as an important but nomenclaturally challenging subject and sets expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual and molecular framework for understanding complement as a cascade centred on C3 activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition generates enough surface-bound C3 activity to trigger complement.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement promotes pathogen elimination through its downstream effector mechanisms.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activation to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects the functions of individual complement components to the clinical effects of their deficiency.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines bacterial strategies for circumventing complement, including how the antibody-binding activity of one evasion protein is exploited clinically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
